2. A native bound on rare output regions

The balance promise can fail at some outcomes. It is nevertheless possible to bound the geometry of those outcomes without assuming unitality or a known invariant state.

For arbitrary supplied POVMs, aggregate the initially rare labels:

 $A_i=
\sum_{x:\,p_i(x)<\lambda t_i(x)}M_i(x).$ Then

 $0\le A_i\le I,
\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}(A_i\rho_i)\le\lambda.$ Aggregating is essential: bounds on individual label probabilities would not control their union when the alphabet is large.

Let  $R$  denote the random set of sites whose final outcomes belong to this rare class. For every fixed set  $S$  and every  $z\ge1$ , I obtain

 $\boxed{
\Pr(S\subseteq R)\le q(z)^{|S|},
} \tag{6}$ where

 $q(z)=
\left(\lambda+\frac{1-\lambda}{z}\right)
\exp\!\left\{
T\left[
2dJz^{k/2}
+\gamma(z-1)
+d\gamma\eta_{\max}z^k
\right]\right\}. \tag{7}$ This holds for the actual general-GKLS scheduled model.

Derivation

Set

 $W_i=I+(z-1)A_i,\qquad
F_S(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(W_S\rho_t).$ The product preparation gives

 $F_S(0)\le[1+(z-1)\lambda]^{|S|}.$ Conjugating each local adjoint term by  $W_S^{-1/2}$  bounds its relative contribution. A touching Hamiltonian term contributes at most  $2Jz^{k/2}$ , a touching perturbation at most  $\gamma\eta_{\max}z^k$ , and a native replacement term at most  $\gamma(z-1)$ . Trace preservation eliminates terms disjoint from  $S$ . Thus

 $F'_S(t)\le |S|
\left[
2dJz^{k/2}+\gamma(z-1)+d\gamma\eta_{\max}z^k
\right]F_S(t).$ Gronwall’s inequality and  $zA_i\le W_i$  give (6).

For sufficiently short dimensionless time  $\tau=\gamma T$ , an explicit choice of  $z$  yields

 $q\le e\left[
\lambda+
\max\left\{
(6dg\tau)^{2/k},\,
3\tau,\,
(3d\eta_{\max}\tau)^{1/k}
\right\}
\right]. \tag{8}$ If the chosen fixed-range lattice graph has at most  $b_{\rm geom}^{m-1}$  connected  $m$ -site sets rooted at a site, then

 $\Pr(\text{some rare component has size}\ge L)
\le n\,b_{\rm geom}^{L-1}q^L. \tag{9}$ When  $b_{\rm geom}q<1$ ,  $L=O(\log(n/\epsilon))$  suffices.

Why this is not yet a sampler

Equation (6) is an unconditional fixed-set estimate. It does not establish independent rare flags or remain valid after arbitrary other outcomes have been pinned.

Small rare regions can still interact through ordinary sites and Hamiltonian-mediated histories. Computing them independently does not establish the relative normalization
